newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST- UK UNIT TO BOOST BARLOW YEAR SHR.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST- UK UNIT TO BOOST BARLOW YEAR SHR.

text.p: A strong contribution from its offshore operations will be the driving force behind a strong growth in year profits at South African diversified industrial conglomerate, Barlow Ltd, analysts said on Thursday.

They said a robust 30 percent rise in pre-tax profits announced last week by UK-based J. Bibby and Sons Plc would translate into an even more sizeable contribution due to a weaker rand/sterling exchange rate.
"Bibby is the star performer...It is in the right markets overseas, and there is the currency benefit," said Mark Ingham, an analyst at brokerage Frankel Pollak.
The rand has lost about 40 percent of its value against the British pound this year.

Analysts polled by Reuters expect Barlows earnings before exceptional items to rise to between 325 and 330 cents per share with a consensus of 326.7 cents -- a 26 percent improvement on last year's 259.7.
The company is due to report results for the year to end-September on Monday.
Barlow's capital equipment division, which is involved in earthmoving and materials handling, was also seen having had a solid second half, analysts said.
"There is a big benefit coming through from the first half, and opencast mining has been a big kicker," an analyst said.
Ingham said: "We are expecting the percentage contribution from capital equipment in the past year to increase nicely."
Finance operations, involving the lease of heavy machinery and cars, was another winner, analysts predicted.
But building and painting interests were expected to have been knocked by little delivery from the government's housing programme.
"There is nothing happening on the building front. Six months ago Federated-Blaikie Ltd was already finding things very bad and nothing has improved," Ingham said.

Consumer electronics division Barcep, which has had a tough few years due to the steady inflow of illegal imports, would show little improvement -- and neither would the motor retailing division, analysts said.
"Grey imports are still there and they (Barcep) have also gone through a big restructure," one analyst said.
Little help would come from the group's listed cement and lime subsidiary, Pretoria Portland Cement Ltd which last week reported flat year earnings, slightly below analysts' expectations.
